title: Telemetry operator & VPC observability runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working runbook for deploying and upgrading a telemetry/observability stack inside customer VPCs and on-prem clusters. Focus is Prometheus/Grafana, OpenTelemetry collectors, and log shipping (s3/forwarders). It targets two audiences: internal deploy engineers (solutions/prof services) and eng teams owning private-deploy TF modules.

Goals / constraints:
- Provide a minimal opinionated operator-based install path that works for air-gapped and VPC-connected installs.
- Keep Terraform surface small: a module per component (prometheus-operator, grafana-provision, otel-collector, log-forwarder).
- Support in-place upgrades with canary/rolling strategy and fast rollback.
- Surface sizing guidance and smoke-test checklist to validate observability readiness.
- Minimize cardinality and storage costs; follow Redwood defaults for retention & remote_write.

High-level architecture (textual):
- Kubernetes cluster (customer managed) inside VPC.
- Prometheus Operator (k8s-operator) managing Prometheus, Alertmanager, ServiceMonitors.
- Grafana provisioned with operator/Helm provisioning (dashboards as configmaps/CRs).
- OpenTelemetry Collector (DaemonSet or Deployment based on workload) -> processing -> exporters (remote_write, s3, kafka).
- Log forwarding layer: fluent-bit as DaemonSet -> compress -> s3/kafka (configurable).
- Optional: Thanos/Cortex sidecar for long-term metrics storage (remote_write gateway).

Operator vs Helm tradeoffs (short):
- Operator: favors CR-driven lifecycle, easier lifecycle hooks for upgrades, better for managed policies.
- Helm: simpler for single-shot installs, less flexible for live reconciliation.
Recommendation: use operator for Prometheus and Grafana in production private deploys; use Helm for OTEL collector that we treat as a plain deployment to allow rapid config iteration.

Terraform module surface (proto):
- Module: telemetry-prom-operator
  - inputs (vars): k8s_namespace, prometheus_replicas, storage_class, retention_days, pvc_size_gb, node_selector, tolerations, scrape_interval
  - outputs: prometheus_instance_name, service_account_name, monitoring_sa_iam_role
- Module: telemetry-grafana
  - inputs: grafana_admin_password_secret_id, dashboard_configmap_names, datasource_remote_write_url, enable_provisioning
  - outputs: grafana_url, grafana_service_ip
- Module: telemetry-otel-collector
  - inputs: collector_replicas, pipeline_processors(list), exporters(list), enable_kubelet_auth
  - outputs: collector_daemonset_name
- Module: telemetry-log-forwarder
  - inputs: forwarder_backends (s3|kafka|elastic), buffer_size_mb, compress(true|false), kms_key_id
  - outputs: forwarder_daemonset_name, s3_bucket_name

Module notes / implementation details:
- Keep Terraform change small: modules should only create K8s CRs or HelmRelease resources, not assume cluster-level plumbing. Less privilege = safer.
- Use K8s provider with impersonation when running from customer-owned state (avoid long-lived SA tokens in TF state).
- Store secrets (grafana admin, s3 creds) in customer KMS-backed secrets (sealed-secrets or SOPS) rather than raw TF variables. Document how to inject these at bootstrap.
- Modules expose "image_overrides" map so we can pin to internal images for air-gapped installs.

Prometheus config guidance:
- Default scrape_interval: 30s for node/system metrics, 15s for infra-critical endpoints (ingress, runtime).
- Reduce high-cardinality labels: remove request-id/session-id from metrics, use labels sparingly. Add relabel_configs to drop dynamic labels.
- PV sizing heuristic: retention_days * ingested_series_rate * series_size_factor. Start conservative: 90GB per 7d for small clusters.
- Remote_write: prefer gateway (Cortex/Thanos) for long-term; if exporting to hosted Redwood metrics, use TLS with mTLS and IP whitelisting.

Grafana provisioning notes:
- Provision dashboards via configmap CRs tracked in Git (dashboards-as-code).
- Enable read-only API tokens for dashboards used by internal health checks.
- Lock down admin user creation; integrate with SSO in non-air-gapped deployments.

OTEL Collector (example pipeline):
- receivers: otlp (grpc/http), prometheus (for scraping when needed)
- processors: batch, memory_limiter (limit: 400MB for 2cpu), probabilisticsampler(rate=0.05) for traces
- exporters: otlp/remote_write -> remote_metrics_gateway, kafka(acks=all,compress=gzip) -> log-archiver
- routing: use attributes to split telemetry to metrics vs traces vs logs exporters
- config example fragment:
  receivers:
    otlp:
      protocols:
        grpc: {}
        http: {}
  processors:
    batch: {}
    memory_limiter:
      limit_mib: 400
      spike_limit_mib: 128
  exporters:
    logging: {}
    otlp/remote_write:
      endpoint: https://metrics-gateway.internal:443
      tls:
        ca_file: /etc/ssl/certs/custom-ca.pem

DaemonSet vs Sidecar guidance for collectors:
- Use DaemonSet for logs/infra metrics (one per node) to reduce cardinality and resource duplication.
- Use sidecar for per-pod tracing when you need per-service sampling/attribution.
- Sidecar increases pod memory/cpu; prefer eBPF-based scraping for host metrics where available.

Log shipping and storage:
- Fluent-bit config: forward -> buffer_queue_limit 64 -> buffer_chunk_size 8k -> compress gzip -> s3 multipart upload (10MB parts)
- Retention: keep raw logs for 30d in S3-standard or on-prem object store, then transition to infrequent-access and archive after 90d.
- If customer requires on-prem archival, support NFS/MinIO with lifecycle rules.

Upgrade plan (Prometheus operator example):
1) Precheck (automation): run sanity script that verifies resource quotas, PVC utilization, CRD versions, and exporter compatibility.
2) Create canary namespace "observability-canary" and deploy updated operator image with a single Prometheus CR pointing at limited targets. Run 1–2 days of smoke metrics.
3) If canary passes, schedule rolling upgrades per AZ: patch operator deployment (strategy: rollout pause at 1 pod) then reconcile Prometheus CRs.
4) Monitor alerts: API availability, scrape errors, target up/down, WAL corruption rates.
5) If degrade, rollback operator image via HelmRelease revision or restore CRD to previous.
6) Post-upgrade: run data validation (compare series counts and remote_write ack rates).

Rollback and recovery notes:
- Prometheus TSDB can be fragile on major upgrades. If WAL corruption suspected: stop writes, snapshot head, restore from snapshots. Keep automated backup (Thanos sidecar snapshots or remote_write backup).
- For DB/storage issues, have documented steps to attach extra PVC and run prometheus --storage.tsdb.wal-segment-size config.

Testing / smoke checklist (pre-deploy and post-upgrade):
- [ ] CRDs registered and CRD versions match expected semver
- [ ] Prometheus targets show <1% scrape_errors in 30m window
- [ ] Prometheus rules evaluate successfully (alerts firing baseline)
- [ ] Remote_write throughput stable and acks >99%
- [ ] Grafana dashboards render and data queries successful (10 sample dashboards)
- [ ] OTEL collector pipelines show <1% dropped spans in 1h test trace
- [ ] Fluent-bit outbound success rate >99% and S3 multipart completes

SRE run commands / quick checks:
- Check Prometheus pods and WAL status:
  kubectl -n monitoring get sts,pvc,po
  kubectl -n monitoring exec -it prometheus-0 -- ls /prometheus/wal
- Collector health endpoints:
  curl -sS http://collector:13133/health | jq .
- Grafana provisioning status (K8s CR): kubectl -n monitoring get grafanadashboards

Security and compliance notes:
- Use KMS/HSM for s3 encryption keys in regulated environments. Document key rotation procedure.
- Audit logs: enable audit webhook to forward to a separate secure logging pipeline with write-once storage.
- RBAC: limit Grafana admin to specific SSO groups; use read-only tokens for automation.

Operational recommendations / heuristics:
- Start with low retention for Prometheus (7d) and scale to 30d only if remote_write enabled.
- Default prometheus replica: 2 for HA but beware of double-scrape duplication when ServiceMonitors are not de-duplicated; use Thanos sidecar for dedupe.
- Use relabel_configs to drop high-card labels before ingest.
- Cap per-node collector memory (memory_limiter) and monitor OOMKill rates after deploy.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide on default remote_write gateway: Cortex vs Thanos vs hosted Redwood endpoint. (Action: product/metrics to own decision)
- Define exact PVC sizing formula and add helper script into TF module to estimate. (Action: infra/observability)
- Air-gapped bootstrap flow: currently using image_overrides, need recipe for sealed-secrets + offline bundle. (Action: eng-sre)

Appendix: quick Terraform snippet for K8s provider impersonation:
provider "kubernetes" {
  host                   = var.cluster_endpoint
  token                  = data.external.kube_token.result.token
  load_config_file       = false
  cluster_ca_certificate = base64decode(var.cluster_ca)
}

Notes for solutions engineers: keep the runbook printed and annotated during customer installs. This doc is intentionally prescriptive but will change as we gather field feedback.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-15: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-12-08: added canary upgrade steps and OTEL memory limits (Ben)
- 2026-01-12: fleshed out Terraform module interface and smoke checklist (Marisol)
